quizzes.stem: A CI step runs Claude Code unattended, and each issue it reports must be posted as an inline note. Which flags make the reply usable for that?

options.a: `--output-format text` with a prompt asking for a bulleted list
options.b: `--max-turns` with a high limit so that the list is complete
options.d: `--bare` alone, which formats replies for scripts

explanation.c: The schema makes the answer a validated object in `structured_output`.
explanation.a: Ruled out because text leaves the entries to be parsed from prose, and "a decision made on prose is a guess".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a limit bounds the loop and does not shape the answer: "The run exits with an error at the limit".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the flag controls what the run loads, with "no hooks, skills, MCP servers, memory or CLAUDE.md", and formats nothing.

quizzes.stem: A review run ends with the subtype `success`, yet the object holds no `structured_output`. What should the job do?

options.a: Fail, because no valid answer exists
options.b: Pass, since the run reports success
options.c: Retry the same request until a value appears
options.d: Pass, with a note that nothing was reported

explanation.a: A run without a valid answer is a failure whatever its subtype says.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the documentation says "Treat that case as a failure as well".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Retrying inside the job repeats cost with no reason to expect a different result".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A job never passes by saying nothing", and a silent pass cannot be told from a failed run.

quizzes.stem: A review job runs on every push and keeps posting remarks that the author has already fixed. What fixes it?

options.a: Raise the turn limit so that the run can compare with earlier comments
options.b: Put earlier reports in the prompt and ask for new issues only
options.c: Tell the reviewer to be more conservative about what it reports
options.d: Run the review inside the session that wrote the change

explanation.b: A run has no memory of the last one, so what was reported must be in the prompt.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A CI run does not remember the last one", and a longer loop does not change that.
explanation.c: Ruled out because such wording does not change what a reviewer reports, since vague instructions "leave the threshold unstated".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the writing session is "less effective at reviewing its own changes" and still would not know what was said on earlier pushes.

quizzes.stem: A job that drafts additional checks keeps proposing situations that are already exercised. What belongs in its prompt?

options.a: A request for many more checks so that coverage becomes certain
options.b: The production code alone, to keep the whole prompt short
options.c: A lower turn limit, so that fewer proposals come back at all
options.d: The test files that exist, plus a request to skip covered cases

explanation.d: The remedy is to show the run what the suite already covers.
explanation.a: Ruled out because more proposals add duplicates, while the aim is "so that suggestions do not duplicate covered scenarios".
explanation.b: Ruled out because without the tests the run cannot see what is covered: "put the existing tests in the prompt".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a record of earlier work carried by the prompt "is the only state the pipeline has", and a turn limit adds none.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5, Claude Code for continuous integration. A team runs Claude Code in CI to review pull requests and to suggest tests. A team asks the same session that wrote a change to review it afterwards, and the verdicts are nearly always approvals. Which change fits?

options.a: Ask the same session to think harder before it approves
options.b: Give the session the full history of the change to review against
options.c: Start a separate run that receives only the diff and the criteria
options.d: Lower the number of turns so that the session decides faster

explanation.c: An independent run sees the change without the reasoning that produced it.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the writing session is "less effective at reviewing its own changes", and more effort does not remove the bias.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a reviewer "sees only the diff and the criteria you give it, not the reasoning that produced the change".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the independent run is a separate invocation, not a second pass in the same conversation".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5, Claude Code for continuous integration. A team runs Claude Code in CI to review pull requests and to suggest tests. A job runs `claude --bare -p`, and its reviews ignore the testing and severity rules that sit in the repository's `CLAUDE.md`. What is the cause and the fix?

options.a: The file is too long, so cut it until it fits the prompt
options.b: Headless runs read the file only on the first push of a branch
options.c: The rules need a `paths` header before a headless run applies them
options.d: That mode skips it, so supply it with `--append-system-prompt-file`

explanation.d: Bare mode skips CLAUDE.md, so the criteria must be passed in by hand.
explanation.a: Ruled out because length is not the issue: "In a bare run the file is passed explicitly" and otherwise it is not read at all.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A CI run does not remember the last one", and no first-push behaviour exists.
explanation.c: Ruled out because no header is involved, and "a bare run without it reviews with no criteria at all, and nothing says so".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5, Claude Code for continuous integration. A team runs Claude Code in CI to review pull requests and to suggest tests. The policy keeps findings at medium severity or above, disables the style category, and fails the job on high findings. A valid run returns one high style finding and one low bug finding. What does the job do?

options.a: It passes and posts no comment
options.b: It fails, because a high finding exists
options.c: It passes and posts the low bug as a comment
options.d: It fails, because a finding in a disabled category counts as an error

explanation.a: The high finding is dropped with its category and the low one falls below the floor, so nothing is kept.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "categories the team disabled are dropped", so the high style finding cannot fail the job.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "findings below a floor are dropped", and a low finding is below a medium floor.
explanation.d: Ruled out because only "a kept finding at a failing severity" fails the job, and a disabled category is dropped before that.

quizzes.stem: A team needs a nightly triage of its issue tracker to run while every laptop is shut. Which setup fits?

options.a: A fixed loop started by an engineer before leaving for the day
options.b: A routine, set up once with a schedule trigger in the cloud
options.c: A desktop task on the laptop of one engineer on the team
options.d: A monitor that watches the tracker through the whole night

explanation.b: The page says routines "keep working when your laptop is closed", and a routine can carry a schedule trigger and connectors.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Tasks only fire while Claude Code is running and idle."
explanation.c: Ruled out because a desktop task "only fires while the app is open and your computer is awake", and every laptop is shut.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a watch has "5 minutes by default, at most 30 minutes" and cannot last a night.

quizzes.stem: A migration has dozens of failing call sites. An engineer wants Claude to keep working without being prompted until the build is clean and the checks pass, and then to stop. Which fits?

options.a: A goal that a separate model evaluates after every turn
options.b: A fixed loop that sends the same prompt every ten minutes
options.c: A monitor that streams the compiler output into the chat
options.d: A routine that starts a fresh cloud session each hour

explanation.a: The page says that after each turn "a model checks whether the condition holds" and that the goal clears when it is met.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a loop's next turn starts when "a time interval elapses" and not when a check holds.
explanation.c: Ruled out because Monitor only "feeds each output line back to Claude" and has a deadline, so it neither continues the work nor stops on a condition.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a routine starts each run from a fresh clone, and "Routines execute on Anthropic-managed cloud infrastructure" from a fresh clone, so they never continue the engineer's own session.

quizzes.stem: An engineer starts `/loop 20m /verify`. At the first fire Claude replied in general terms and nothing was exercised. What is the cause?

options.a: The interval is too short for a loop to launch any skill, bundled or custom, at all
options.b: That bundled skill forbids model invocation, the only kind a scheduled prompt runs
options.c: A loop re-runs prompts only and never starts a bundled skill, whatever its settings
options.d: The session was not restored after the first fire, so the loop lost its task entirely

explanation.b: The page says that skills marked `disable-model-invocation: true`, the bundled `/verify` among them, reach Claude as plain text, because "A scheduled fire only runs skills that Claude is allowed to invoke on its own."
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Any interval from one minute upwards is allowed", and 20 minutes is well above it.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a loop can run "A prompt, or a skill", for example `/review-pr 1234`, which Claude may invoke on its own.
explanation.d: Ruled out because loops on a fixed interval "keep running until you cancel them", and nothing in the session ended here.
